body: The Wyoming Supreme Court on February 2, 2026 revived a $14 million lawsuit by Gunwerks, LLC, a maker of custom guns and optics, over the manufacturing facility built for it in Cody, Cowboy State Daily reported. In a unanimous opinion by Justice Bridget Hill, Gunwerks, LLC v. Forward Cody Wyoming, Inc., 2026 WY 16, the court reversed the Park County District Court's dismissal of Gunwerks' claims against architect Plan One Architects and contractor Sletten Construction of Wyoming, Inc., and also reversed its grant of summary judgment to Forward Cody Wyoming, Inc.

Because only a community could receive money from the Wyoming Business Council's Business Ready Communities program, Gunwerks worked with the City of Cody and Forward Cody, a nonprofit economic development group, to obtain a $3 million grant and a $3 million loan for the building, according to the opinion and Cowboy State Daily. Gunwerks provided the land and was to lease the facility from Forward Cody with an option to buy it. Forward Cody hired Plan One to design the facility and Sletten to build it; Gunwerks signed neither contract.

Gunwerks alleges the finished building had poor climate control, pervasive water leaks, a failing shooting tunnel and crumbling concrete, and the opinion notes a 157-page punch list of construction issues. Gunwerks sued Forward Cody in 2021 and added the architect and contractor in 2022, Cowboy State Daily reported. Forward Cody disputes the $14 million figure, which its brief says includes $7.44 million in what it calls speculative lost profits from a six-month shutdown, and argues Gunwerks tried to take control of the project. Plan One argued it owed Gunwerks no contractual duty.

Justice Hill wrote that the city and Forward Cody "did not, one day, randomly decide to build a generic building," and that Gunwerks had negotiated with them to build it a custom manufacturing facility. The court held that Gunwerks had pleaded enough to proceed as an intended third-party beneficiary of the Plan One and Sletten contracts, and that Forward Cody had more duties than managing the $6 million. The case returns to the Park County District Court.

timeline.label: Gunwerks, Forward Cody and the City of Cody sign the development agreement for the facility
Gunwerks adds Plan One and Sletten as defendants
Wyoming Supreme Court reverses the dismissal and the summary judgment and remands to the Park County District Court
